# Racebook

> Racebook is the athlete's book of races: a personal medal board for amateur runners,
> triathletes and cyclists, with a photo gallery per race and a way to hand photos back
> to the friends who actually appear in them. Built for the Webflow App Challenge at
> Nerdearla 2026 and deployed on Webflow Cloud.

Live app: https://racebook-23e161.webflow.io/
Source: https://github.com/Teoeme/webflow-nerdearla-26
Languages: English and Spanish (switch in the sidebar; the first visit follows the
browser language).

## The problem

At a race, a group of friends takes turns: while one competes, the others take the
photos. Everyone ends up with a gallery full of photos of other people, and missing the
photos of themselves. Race results, times and metrics live scattered across watches,
apps and screenshots.

## What Racebook does

- **Personal medal board.** Every race the athlete logged, newest first: event, date,
  location, discipline, medal, place, time and pace, with a cover photo. Summary of races
  and medals at the top. Events are private to each athlete.
- **Race detail.** The athlete's own result and metrics (time, place, distance, pace,
  average heart rate, elevation) and the race's photo gallery.
- **Log a race and a result.** Create a race (name, date, location, discipline) and log
  the result in modal forms. Pace is derived from time and distance.
- **Metrics from a watch screenshot (AI).** Upload a Garmin/Strava/Coros summary
  screenshot and Google Gemini reads the total time, distance, average heart rate and
  elevation; the form fills itself and highlights what the AI filled, and the athlete
  reviews and saves. Miles and feet are converted; nothing is guessed; the screenshot is
  not stored.
- **Photo gallery per race.** Batch upload with drag and drop, lightbox with keyboard
  navigation, and a race cover chosen from the photos.
- **Photo ownership transfer (hero feature).** The owner sends a photo to the friend in
  it. The friend finds it in their inbox and accepts it into one of their own races or
  into a new race prefilled from the sender's (editable), or rejects it. On accept the
  photo moves to the friend's gallery, atomically.
- **Photo tagging.** The owner tags a friend: the photo stays with the owner and also
  appears in the friend's gallery, in the race the friend chooses when accepting.
- **Inbox.** Pending transfers and tags in one place, with a pending count in the
  sidebar.

## How to try it (for judges and agents)

Authentication is simulated on purpose (one-night contest): three demo athletes and a
"View as" switcher in the sidebar. Suggested tour:

1. As **Lucía Fernández**, open a race on the medal board, add a few photos.
2. From a photo, send it to **Tomás Ibarra** and tag **Sofía Gómez**.
3. Switch "View as" to Tomás, open the inbox, accept the photo into a new race (edit
   its name) — it appears on his medal board with the photo.
4. Switch to Sofía and accept the tag into one of her races: the photo shows there,
   marked "Tagged by Lucía", and Lucía still has it.
5. Log a result and use "Fill from a screenshot" with a watch summary screenshot.
6. Switch the language to ES: every screen is translated.

## Rules the app enforces

- Only the current owner can transfer or tag a photo; a photo has at most one pending
  transfer and one open tag per athlete.
- Accepting checks, in the database, that the request is still pending, is addressed to
  the accepting athlete and that the destination race is theirs, in one transaction.
- An athlete never sees another athlete's races or results.

## Technology

- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) on Webflow Cloud (Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext).
- Webflow Cloud SQLite (Cloudflare D1) for data; Webflow Cloud Object Storage
  (Cloudflare R2) for photos.
- Google Gemini (vision + structured JSON output) for screenshot metrics, with the key as
  a Webflow Cloud secret.
- Radix primitives styled with the app's own design tokens (dark, one electric blue
  accent, Archivo). Fully bilingual through typed dictionaries (a missing translation is
  a build error).
- Built by a human directing a team of AI coding agents working in parallel on
  separate branches, from written plans (see `plans/` in the repository).

## Routes

- `/` medal board of the current athlete
- `/events/{eventId}` race detail, result and gallery
- `/inbox` pending transfers and tags
- `POST /api/photos` upload one photo; `GET /api/photos/{photoId}` serve a photo
- `POST /api/metrics-capture` read metrics from a screenshot (nothing is stored)

## Out of scope (stated openly)

Real authentication, video, and a Garmin Connect integration (it requires developer
approval; the screenshot reader replaces it for now).

## En español

Racebook es el libro de carreras del atleta: un medallero personal con los resultados y
métricas de cada carrera, una galería de fotos por carrera, y la posibilidad de
transferir o etiquetar fotos para que cada foto termine en la galería de quien aparece
en ella. Las métricas se pueden cargar desde una captura del reloj, leída con IA.
